Install: Cypress is an open-source end-to-end testing framework installed via npm. It includes its own test runner, assertion library, and browser control.
npm install cypress --save-dev && npx cypress open
Test Structure: Cypress tests use Mocha-style describe/it blocks. Tests run in a real browser with automatic waiting, DOM snapshotting, and time-travel debugging.
Assertions: Cypress bundles Chai assertions with should and expect syntax. Assertions automatically retry until the element meets the condition or times out.

get: cy.get selects elements by CSS selectors, returning a jQuery-wrapped element. It supports chaining and built-in retry-ability.
find: cy.find scopes the selection to descendants of a previously yielded element. It is ideal for navigating within a specific container.
contains: cy.contains selects elements by their text content, which is more resilient to DOM structure changes than CSS selectors.
Best Practices: Use data-* attributes like data-cy for robust selectors that resist CSS and text changes. Avoid brittle selectors tied to implementation details.

click: cy.click simulates a mouse click on a DOM element. It supports options like multiple clicks, position offsets, and force-clicking hidden elements.
type: cy.type simulates keyboard input into form fields character by character. It supports special keys via curly braces like {enter}.
select: cy.select picks an option from a <select> element by value, text, or index. It supports multiple selection when the multiple attribute is present.
hover: cy.invoke with trigger simulates hover events since Cypress lacks a native hover command. It shows hidden menus and tooltips.

Intercept: cy.intercept spies on and modifies HTTP requests at the network level. It can stub responses, wait for requests, and assert on request details.
Mock: Request stubbing returns static data instead of hitting the real server, making tests fast, deterministic, and independent of backend availability.
Wait: cy.wait pauses test execution until a specific aliased network request completes. It can also wait for a specified amount of time.
Stub: Stubbing replaces server responses entirely, useful for testing edge cases, loading states, and error handling without a real server.

Fixtures: Fixtures are external data files (JSON, images, etc.) stored in cypress/fixtures. They provide realistic test data that can be reused across tests.
Custom Commands: Custom commands wrap reusable logic into chainable Cypress commands via Cypress.Commands.add, improving test readability and reducing duplication.
Test Data: Test data factories generate consistent, repeatable data for tests. Using beforeEach hooks ensures a clean state before each test run.

Screenshots: Cypress automatically captures screenshots on test failure. Manual screenshots can be taken with cy.screenshot for visual documentation.
Videos: Cypress records video of the entire test run. Videos are stored in cypress/videos and can be configured or disabled in cypress.config.js.
CI Integration: Cypress runs headlessly in CI with cypress run. The Cypress GitHub Action or Docker image provides browsers and dependencies.

Mount: Component testing mounts individual components in isolation using cy.mount. It requires the @cypress/react or @cypress/vue adapter.
Props: Props are passed directly to the mounted component to test different states and configurations without needing the full application.
Events: Event callbacks can be verified using Cypress spies. cy.spy wraps a function and tracks whether it was called with expected arguments.

Page Objects: Page Objects encapsulate page-specific selectors and actions into reusable classes, reducing test duplication and insulating tests from UI changes.
class LoginPage { visit() { cy.visit('/login'); } fillEmail(v) { cy.get('[data-cy=email]').type(v); } submit() { cy.get('[data-cy=submit]').click(); } }
Real World: Real-world E2E tests simulate complete user journeys like signup, purchase, or search. They test critical business flows from start to finish.
it('completes checkout', () => { cy.visit('/'); cy.contains('Buy').click(); cy.contains('Checkout').click(); cy.get('[data-cy=card]').type('4242'); });
Debugging: Cypress debugging tools include cy.pause to halt execution, cy.debug to log the current subject, and browser DevTools for interactive inspection.
